entries.title: II Kings 20:1
segments:
Sick unto death; with a deadly disease. 
 
In every situation men are liable to sickness and death.  The should therefore have all their affairs so arranged, as to be habitually prepared to leave this world and enter on the retributions of eternity.

entries.title: II Kings 20:5
segments: Prayer is often a means of removing sickness which would otherwise prove mortal, and inducing the Lord to continue life when he would otherwise have taken it away.

entries.title: II Kings 20:7
segments:
The boil; with which Hezekiah was aflicted, and which, if God had not interposed, would have been mortal. 
 
The fact that diseases are God's servants, and that they come and go at his bidding, should never supersede the use of appropriate means, or lead us in any measure to neglect them.

entries.title: II Kings 20:9
segments: The shadow; the shadow on the sun-dial,

entries.title: II Kings 20:11
segments: The Lord gives abundant evidence of the truth of his promises, that his people may trust his word without fear of being disappointed.

entries.title: II Kings 20:13
segments: Showed them all the house of his precious things--all that was found in his treasures; in this he was manifestly elated with vanity, and God accordingly forewarned him of the judgments that should come from Babylon upon his family.  Compare

. 
 
Even good men are liable to be elated with their blessings, to seek applause, and so display their acquisitions as to displease the Lord.

entries.title: II Kings 20:16
segments: The Lord will effectually humble the pride of his people, take off their hearts from transitory, uncertain riches, and lead them to trust alone in Him who giveth them richly all things to enjoy, and who can at any time take away what his has given.

entries.title: II Kings 20:18
segments: Thy sons; that is, thy descendants.  The threatening was literally fulfilled in the case of Daniel and his companions, who were "of the king's seed."

entries.title: II Kings 20:19
segments: However trying the dispensations of Providence, pious men will submit to them; knowing that God has the best of reasons for all which he does, and doeth all things well.
